posts.text:
My prediction for software engineering over the next 3 to 5 years.

Computer science and software engineering fundamentals will become far more valuable than knowing the latest frameworks.

If AI can write code in almost any language, knowing the nuance of another framework becomes less of a competitive advantage.

But understanding algorithms, data structures, networking, operating systems, databases, architecture and security?

That's a different story.

You still need to know:

 - Why a particular architecture is appropriate.
 - Why an API might fail.
 - Why a database won't scale.
 - Why an apparently working solution might be insecure.

A coding agent can build a solution.

But you need the knowledge to evaluate the trade-offs and recognise when it's wrong.

So, I think we'll see a renewed emphasis on the fundamentals of computer science and software engineering.

TL/DR: Learning how computers and software systems work will matter more than memorising how to use them.

What do you think?
